caption: What if you climbed the chilli ladder? Chilli heat is measured in Scoville Heat Units (SHU). Shimla mirch scores zero. A jalapeño reaches up to about 8,000. Guntur chillies from Andhra Pradesh hit around 35,000 to 40,000. Then comes Northeast India's bhut jolokia at about 1 million SHU, named the world's hottest chilli by Guinness in 2007. Nagaland's Naga Mircha even has its own GI tag. The Carolina Reaper later took the crown at 1.64 million, and since 2023 Pepper X holds the record at 2.69 million. Pure capsaicin, the chemical behind the burn, tops the scale at 16 million, a lab-only substance. Please never dare anyone to eat super-hot chillies. Plot twist: chilli isn't even Indian. It came from the Americas, and the Portuguese brought it to India after Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in 1498. Nagaland's Hornbill Festival starts 1 December. How high on the ladder can YOU go? 👇
